baseline_facts.content: Patient is forty eight years old.
Patient has diarrhea for the past three days.
Diarrhea occurs five to six times a day.
No visible blood in stools reported.
Vomited a couple of times at the beginning.
Has eaten little solid food recently.
Felt a bit warm at the beginning of illness.
No known contact with people with diarrhea in the last week.
Father died of bowel cancer about ten years ago.
Has taken time off work in the last three days due to illness.
Doctor advised drinking plenty of fluids.
Doctor recommended Dioralyte for fluid replacement.
Doctor advised taking paracetamol if feeling feverish and weak.
Doctor advised to remain off work for the next day or two.
Doctor advised to be diarrhea-free for about twenty four to forty eight hours before returning to work.
Doctor advised to return next week if not better.

candidate_facts.content: Patient reports very bad diarrhoea for approximately 3 days.
Two episodes of vomiting occurred at onset.
Patient felt mildly febrile at onset.
Patient denies visible blood in stool.
Patient recalls no unsafe food exposures.
Patient reports no contacts with similar illness.
No aggravating or relieving factors specified.
No prior evaluations or treatment for current illness.
Patient uses salbutamol (blue inhaler) as needed for asthma.
Salbutamol dose, route, and frequency not documented.
Father died from bowel cancer approximately 10 years ago.
Patient has been off work for the last 3 days due to illness.
Patient drinks alcohol socially and infrequently.
Physical exam not performed or not documented.
No diagnostics available during this encounter.
Differential diagnosis includes bacterial or food-borne gastroenteritis.
Differential diagnosis includes early inflammatory bowel disease, considered less likely.
No culprit drugs identified for medication-induced diarrhoea.
Patient is at risk of dehydration.
Patient advised to increase oral fluids.
Oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte) advised per packet instructions.
Paracetamol 500-1000 mg orally every 6 hours as needed for fever or malaise.
Patient advised to remain off work until diarrhoea-free for 24–48 hours.
Patient advised to eat small, bland meals as tolerated.
Education provided on urgent review sign: inability to keep fluids down.
Education provided on urgent review sign: persistent vomiting.
Education provided on urgent review sign: bloody stools.
Education provided on urgent review sign: high fever.
Education provided on urgent review sign: severe abdominal pain.
Education provided on urgent review sign: dizziness or syncope.
Patient advised to track urine output.
Patient advised to aim for clear or light-yellow urine.
Return if symptoms not improving within 5–7 days.
